items.claim: Define the selected finite C2 vertex-spin regulator as a model-data specialization of the finite two-group background interface, including its unit per-background weight and background-only relative convention.
source_uses: Moore–Saxena §23.3, PDF pp. 96–99: finite state spaces, homotopy-cardinality measure, and higher-group construction limitations.
Freed–Quinn §2, PDF pp. 8–11: ordinary finite gauge-groupoid measure and sewing context.
Baez–Lauda §8.3, PDF pp. 54–59: skeletal two-group and associator/pentagon convention.
Benini–Córdova–Hsin §2.3, PDF pp. 18–20: simplicial backgrounds and gauge conventions.
items.argument_disposition: The definition states all local model choices and conventions explicitly. Its proof counts 2^V spin configurations, verifies unit normalization, proves the vertex-label translations are bijections and the constant C2 action is effective, and identifies the finite relative background sum. The local definition and the finite background gauging data are the exact suppliers; the chosen A={0}, beta=0 specialization matches their current interfaces. Literature is contextual and does not substitute for the local construction.

items.claim: Adopt the finite C2 vertex-spin regulator, zero action, normalized uniform measure, unit background response, and the local relative background convention as the physical model for subsequent conditional deductions.

items.argument_disposition: This is explicitly an adopted postulate, not a derived or empirical assertion. The exact configuration and relative conventions are in the preceding local definition. The postulate’s scope expressly excludes continuum and empirical claims.

items.claim: Prove, conditional on the adopted finite spin model, background gauge invariance and the absolute, relative, and gluing formulas for its unit-response finite background gauging amplitudes.

items.argument_disposition: The local proof reindexes finite spin sums by the explicit gauge bijections and invokes the current mathematical finite two-group gluing theorem. The theorem’s hypotheses of finite groups, normalized beta, invariant scalar W=1, exact relative restriction, and ordered subcomplex factorization all match. The background response is derived in this specified model; no universal anomaly or continuum conclusion is claimed.

The relative interval amplitudes equal one and the seam mass equals one-half, reproducing the direct full-path result. The exact gluing theorem applies with unit factorized weight.
